$comment: gzip byte ceilings for dist javascript. Ratchet down as the skeleton matures; raising a budget requires review.

notes.devkit: 5400 -> 6400 (v9.14): the paired report gains the resolution of its own deltas — pairedResolution (Wald interval on the paired difference, the smallest difference the cases could detect at 80% power, and the rule of three when two arms never disagreed) plus casesForEffect, which turns an observed discordance rate into the number of cases a 2pp claim would need. Measured 5352 -> 6281 B gzip over both module formats: about 0.9 KB for a capability the report quotes on every comparison, priced here rather than absorbed silently. The package had 48 B of headroom, so no existing export was near its ceiling and none was removed to pay for this. 6400 -> 6900 (v9.22): the pairing became one function. `pairByOccurrence` returns the aligned pairs and the two leftovers so that `compareArms` and `strata.pairCases` fold over the same alignment — the divergence between them was a real defect: the two readers of one artifact counted 2 pairs where the other counted 3 on a split that repeats a question. Measured 6387 -> 6766 B gzip over both module formats: about 0.4 KB for an exported function and two exported types, which is the price of not keeping two definitions of the same concept. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift; no export was removed to pay for it, because the alternative was leaving the second definition in place.
notes.ai: 35000 -> 36000 (v9.3): the pairwise selector adds a prompt builder, a parser and a knockout loop, about 1.1 KB gzip. Reviewed as a capability rather than drift, and the two prompt builders were merged onto one rules block and one candidate renderer first, which returned 155 B. 36000 -> 39000 (v9.9): the empty-result turn adds the message builder, the blind control's text and the retry loop, plus a second exported builder so the runner continues the same conversation instead of rebuilding it — about 1.6 KB gzip over both module formats. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently. 39000 -> 41000 (v9.13): the decomposition prompt adds a rule block and a reader that takes the last block, plus one exported parser and its step counter — about 0.7 KB gzip per module format, and the ceiling moves by the smallest step that keeps a capability from being absorbed silently. 41000 -> 42000 (v9.21): the per-call meter files each call under the purpose it declared, so a multi-call arm's bill can be read as a table rather than an argument. Measured 40281 -> 41271 B gzip over both module formats: about 1.0 KB for a bucket map, its accumulator and three exported types, after the character and token loops were merged onto one write point and the internal label constant was kept out of the public surface. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently; the ceiling moves by the smallest step that keeps it from being absorbed. 42000 -> 43000 (v9.24): the audit turn — one call that asks the model which of the question's conditions its own statement failed to write, and adopts the statement it writes next. It adds the message builder, the reply counter, the loop that decides whether to keep the rewrite, and a purpose label so the call is billed as its own row instead of disappearing into generation. Measured 41271 -> 42735 B gzip over both module formats: 1,464 B for the only mechanism here aimed at the 16.1-18.8pp of failures no result-based trigger can see. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently; the ceiling moves by the smallest step that keeps it from being absorbed. 43000 -> 45000 (v9.25): the format contract. `replyShape` reads four dimensions off one reply that every reader in this package already depends on — whether it fenced its statement, whether it is nothing but a decorated choice, how many STEP lines it wrote, how many omissions it named — and `formatProfile` turns a sample of them into a verdict per dimension, with a floor of three replies and a nine-in-ten threshold so that one unlucky case cannot flip a strategy. The same change widens the three strict readers (`parseChoiceToken`, the STEP line, the MISSING line) to accept the decoration a model that has never been benchmarked puts around a label it was told to write; on the arms measured here that window changes at most one case in 496, and on an uncalibrated model it is the difference between an unanswered call and a wrong one. Measured 42735 -> 43997 B gzip over both module formats: 1,262 B for the only instrument in this repository that reads a reply before any result exists, and therefore the only one that can predict a backbone collapse instead of reporting it as a lower score. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently. 45000 -> 46500 (v9.26): the request contract. `turnTemperature` is three lines, but `refusalDetail` is the cost: a 4xx body is JSON in three disagreeing shapes, plain text from a proxy, or an empty page, and turning each into one sentence with a 200-character ceiling is ~25 lines in both module formats. The alternative was a provider that reports every refusal as "the endpoint is unreachable", which is the one diagnosis that sends a deployment at the network when the fault is in the request. Paid for here rather than absorbed: measured 43997 -> 45336 B gzip. 46500 -> 48500 (v9.27): the deployment-time adaptation layer. `packages/ai/src/adapt.ts` adds the four bounded strategies as a table, the three layers that choose among them (`probeProtocol` reads a refusal's status and the first reply's shape, `admissible` drops the selector when a model never writes a parseable choice, `chooseStrategy`/`createObserver` switch only when Wilson intervals separate), and `wilson` itself so that the runtime decision and the published report share one definition of "better". Measured 45336 -> 48210 B gzip over both module formats: 2,874 B for the only code in this repository that decides what to run on a model nobody has benchmarked, which the cold-start harness (eval/bird/adapt.ts) then prices at 1.1-1.6pp of regret and declines. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently; no export was removed to pay for it, because the alternative was shipping a default with no way to leave it. 48500 -> 49000 (v9.28): the agreement mark. The selector was shown each candidate's statement, row count, column count and three preview rows, and never the one fact a 2+1 pool turns on — that two of the three returned exactly the same thing — because three hundred characters of a wide result cannot establish equality. The cost is one optional field on `Candidate`, a render line per agreeing candidate, a header line and one rule sentence, plus the two helpers that count distinct results: measured 48210 -> 48754 B gzip over both module formats, 544 B. The block is emitted only when a caller supplies marks, so every arm measured before this one keeps a byte-identical prompt and the ablation prices the information rather than a rewrite. A capability, priced here rather than absorbed silently. 49000 -> 54500 (v9.29): the capability contract. `capability.ts` declares what an endpoint does with a request (family, whether sampling is honoured, whether JSON mode is served, the answer budget, whether the prompt may ask for reasoning), derives it from the model name, and rewrites the request so that a parameter the endpoint discards is removed instead of sent and forgotten. The same change carries the declaration through `withCallCounter`, reports the removal per call and per arm, gives the selector a second instruction for a judge that thinks before it answers, and adds a reader that takes the choice from the final line only when that instruction was sent. Measured 48754 -> 52129 B gzip over both module formats: 3,375 B for the layer that makes "swap the backbone" a decision the pipeline can see, and for the two defects it exposed — a metered provider that dropped the declaration, and a retry turn that rewrote the reasoning model's statement with the chat model. The chat request is byte-identical to the one every published reading was taken with, so no existing number moves and none had to be re-measured to pay for this.
